name: USB-B (USB 2.0, printer)
description: The tall square USB connector on the DEVICE end of a USB 2.0 link -- printers, audio interfaces, older Arduinos (Uno/Mega), USB DACs. Same four USB 2.0 signals as USB-A (VBUS, D-, D+, GND); the different shell just guarantees you plug host-to-device (A-to-B) and can't accidentally join two hosts.
variants: USB 3.0 Type-B is a taller connector (the square with a bump on top) carrying the extra SuperSpeed pins; it accepts a USB 2.0 B plug but not vice-versa. Seen on USB3 docks/drives.
Mini-B and Micro-B are the small device connectors that largely replaced full-size B on portable gear.
gotchas: Same signals as USB-A -- the Type-B shell exists purely to enforce host(A)-to-device(B) cabling. You cannot make an A-to-A or B-to-B USB cable and expect it to work.
Common on class-compliant USB audio interfaces and MIDI devices; a flaky Type-B solder joint (they take mechanical stress) shows up as random disconnects.
Charge-only vs data: as with any USB, a cable missing D+/D- charges but never enumerates.
notes: USB 2.0 Type-B 4-pin (VBUS/D-/D+/GND), same signals as USB-A. Device-end connector.
